description:
What a disaster really looks like, day by day. Seventy-six days in a six-foot raft, four years alone on a Pacific island, the fourteen days after a nuclear strike. Every video runs on a clock.

Each one is built from one record: an accident report, a survivor's own account, a government survival manual. Then it is told as a timeline you can follow. Day 1. Day 9. Day 40. What you eat, what breaks, what most people get wrong, and what the people who walked out did instead.

Two or three long videos a week, and a short one most days.

Made for anyone who has read about a crash at 2am and wanted to know how anybody survived it.

Sources are listed under every video. Nothing here is a prediction, and nothing is pushed past what the record says.

72 Days in the Andes: How 16 Survived the 1972 Plane Crash
